scenes.say: Ever wonder how JavaScript objects share methods? Is it all about prototypes, or do classes play a role?

scenes.label: Prototype
scenes.sub: Objects inherit behavior from their prototype.
scenes.say: First up, prototypes. Every object in JavaScript can inherit features from another object, called its prototype.
Now, classes. With ES6, classes give us a cleaner way to write constructor functions and methods, but under the hood, they still use prototypes.
Prototypes are flexible and lightweight, great for quick sharing. Classes offer structure and built-in constructors, making inheritance easier to manage.

scenes.question: Are classes totally separate from prototypes?
scenes.wrong: Yes, classes are a new system.
scenes.right: No, classes use prototypes behind the scenes.
scenes.say: Interview trap: Are classes a new inheritance system? Nope! They just wrap prototypes with nicer syntax.
